newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Milosevic wins backing for federal presidency bid.
newsitem.headline: Milosevic wins backing for federal presidency bid.

text.p: Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic won Montenegrin support on Monday for his takeover of Yugoslavia's federal presidency, despite a running feud with Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.
Montenegro's ruling DPS party agreed Milosevic would replace outgoing Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic, who steps down on June 26.

Milosevic is expected to assume the federal presidency within weeks, paving the way for presidential elections in Serbia early this autumn. The Serbian constitution forbids him from seeking a third term as the republic's president.

The DPS leadership voted 51-36 in favour of support for Milosevic's switch to the federal office and rejected an attempt by Djukanovic to make its backing conditional on a promise of economic and political reforms.
The federal president is elected by the federal parliament, where Milosevic's ruling Serbian Socialist party SPS and the Montenegrin DPS command a majority of almost two thirds.

The DPS refused to back SPS proposals for constitutional changes under which the federal president would be elected by universal suffrage, on the grounds that the amendment would reduce Montenegro's authority within the federation.
Montenegro currently has equal status with Serbia although it is economically and demographically dwarfed by its partner.
